requirements.original: c) Type mismatch at storing the received value or parts of the received value and storing the sender shall cause an error.
requirements.canonical: A type mismatch at storing the sender in a `trigger` operation SHALL cause an error.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.3 -- c) Type mismatch at storing the received value or parts of the received value and storing the sender shall cause an error.

requirements.original: NOTE 3: An error due to a type mismatch may happen if the types in the receive part are not compatible to the types in the assignment part or, if the from clause is missing, but the type of the sender can be determined and it is not type compatible with the type in the sender clause.
requirements.canonical: A type mismatch error CAN occur if the types in the receive part are not compatible with the types in the assignment part.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.3 -- NOTE 3: An error due to a type mismatch may happen if the types in the receive part are not compatible to the types in the assignment part or, if the from clause is missing, but the type of the sender can be determined and it is not type compatible with the type in the sender clause.

requirements.original: NOTE 3: An error due to a type mismatch may happen if the types in the receive part are not compatible to the types in the assignment part or, if the from clause is missing, but the type of the sender can be determined and it is not type compatible with the type in the sender clause.
requirements.canonical: A type mismatch error CAN occur if the `from` clause is missing but the type of the sender can be determined and is not type compatible with the type in the `sender` clause.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.3 -- NOTE 3: An error due to a type mismatch may happen if the types in the receive part are not compatible to the types in the assignment part or, if the from clause is missing, but the type of the sender can be determined and it is not type compatible with the type in the sender clause.

requirements.original: d) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause C.5) of the port instance referenced in the trigger operation.
requirements.canonical: Every AddressRef item in the `from` clause of a `trigger` operation SHALL be of type `address`, a component type, or the address type bound to the port type of the referenced port instance.

ambiguity.issue: 'component' is used where 'component type' is meant.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.3 -- d) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause C.5) of the port instance referenced in the trigger operation.

requirements.original: d) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause C.5) of the port instance referenced in the trigger operation.
requirements.canonical: Every ValueRef item in the `sender` clause of a `trigger` operation SHALL be of type `address`, a component type, or the address type bound to the port type of the referenced port instance.

ambiguity.issue: 'component' is used where 'component type' is meant.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.3 -- d) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause C.5) of the port instance referenced in the trigger operation.

requirements.original: No AddressRef in the from clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.
requirements.canonical: An AddressRef in the `from` clause of a `trigger` operation SHALL NOT contain the special value `null` at the time of the operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.3 -- No AddressRef in the from clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.

requirements.original: e) The PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized port array.
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef of a `trigger` operation SHALL be a reference to a completely initialized port array.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.3 -- e) The PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized port array.

requirements.original: f) The index redirection shall only be used when the operation is used on an any from port array construct.
requirements.canonical: The index redirection of a `trigger` operation SHALL only be used when the operation is used on an `any from` port array construct.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.3 -- f) The index redirection shall only be used when the operation is used on an any from port array construct.

requirements.original: g) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional port arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective array.
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a single-dimensional port array, the type of the integer variable SHALL allow storing the highest index of the port array.
requirements.condition: index redirection used for single-dimensional port array
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.3 -- g) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional port arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective array.

requirements.original: h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional port arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the size of the integer array or `record of integer` type SHALL be exactly the same as the number of dimensions of the port array.
requirements.condition: index redirection used for multi-dimensional port array

ambiguity.issue: 'the dimension of the respective array' is read as the number of dimensions (supported by example 5: p[10][10] with v_i[2]).
readings: The size of the integer array SHALL equal the number of dimensions of the port array.
The size of the integer array SHALL equal the size of a dimension of the port array.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.3 -- h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional port arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.

requirements.original: h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional port arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the element type of the integer array or `record of integer` type SHALL allow storing the highest index of all dimensions of the port array.
requirements.condition: index redirection used for multi-dimensional port array
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.3 -- h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional port arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.

requirements.original: i) If a variable referenced in the value, sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the trigger operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the trigger operation.
requirements.canonical: If a variable referenced in the `value`, `sender` or `@index` clause of a `trigger` operation is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable IS equal to the result produced by the `trigger` operation.
requirements.condition: the referenced variable is lazy or fuzzy
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.3 -- i) If a variable referenced in the value, sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the trigger operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the trigger operation.

requirements.original: i) If a variable referenced in the value, sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the trigger operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the trigger operation.
requirements.canonical: Later evaluation of a lazy or fuzzy variable assigned in a `trigger` operation redirect SHALL NOT lead to repeated invocation of the `trigger` operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.3 -- i) If a variable referenced in the value, sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the trigger operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the trigger operation.

requirements.original: j) If the trigger operation contains both from and sender clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause shall be type compatible with the template in the from clause.
requirements.canonical: If a `trigger` operation contains both a `from` and a `sender` clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause SHALL be type compatible with the AddressRef in the `from` clause.
requirements.condition: both from and sender clause present

ambiguity.issue: 'template in the from clause' is used although the from clause contains AddressRef items (address or component references), not templates.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.3 -- j) If the trigger operation contains both from and sender clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause shall be type compatible with the template in the from clause.

requirements.original: k) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `trigger` operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.3 -- k) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.original: l) TemplateInstance shall be of a data type.
requirements.canonical: The TemplateInstance of a `trigger` operation SHALL be of a data type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.3 -- l) TemplateInstance shall be of a data type.

requirements.original: m) The @nodefault modifier is allowed only in stand-alone trigger statements.
requirements.canonical: The `@nodefault` modifier SHALL only be used in stand-alone `trigger` statements.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.2.3 -- m) The @nodefault modifier is allowed only in stand-alone trigger statements.

requirements.original: ObjectReference "." call "(" TemplateInstance [ "," ( CallTimerValue | nowait ) ] ")" [ to Address ]
requirements.canonical: The `call` operation has the syntax ObjectReference "." `call` "(" TemplateInstance [ "," ( CallTimerValue | `nowait` ) ] ")" [ `to` Address ].
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- ObjectReference "." call "(" TemplateInstance [ "," ( CallTimerValue | nowait ) ] ")" [ to Address ]

requirements.original: NOTE: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "all component"._
requirements.canonical: The Address of the `to` clause of a `call` operation MAY be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef items or `all component`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- NOTE: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "all component"._

requirements.original: The information to be transmitted in the send part of the call operation is a signature that may either be defined in the form of a signature template or be defined in-line.
requirements.canonical: The information transmitted in the send part of a `call` operation IS a signature that is defined either as a signature template or in-line.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- The information to be transmitted in the send part of the call operation is a signature that may either be defined in the form of a signature template or be defined in-line.

requirements.original: In case of non-blocking procedure-based communication the handling of exceptions to call operations is done by using catch (see clause 22.3.6) operations as alternatives in alt statements.
requirements.canonical: In non-blocking procedure-based communication, exceptions to a `call` operation ARE handled by `catch` operations used as alternatives in `alt` statements.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- In case of non-blocking procedure-based communication the handling of exceptions to call operations is done by using catch (see clause 22.3.6) operations as alternatives in alt statements.

requirements.original: If the nowait option is used, the handling of responses or exceptions to call operations is done by using getreply (see clause 22.3.4) and catch (see clause 22.3.6) operations as alternatives in alt statements.
requirements.canonical: If the `nowait` option is used in a `call` operation, responses and exceptions to the call ARE handled by `getreply` and `catch` operations used as alternatives in `alt` statements.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- If the nowait option is used, the handling of responses or exceptions to call operations is done by using getreply (see clause 22.3.4) and catch (see clause 22.3.6) operations as alternatives in alt statements.

requirements.original: In case of blocking procedure-based communication, the handling of responses or exceptions to a call is done in the response and exception handling part of the call operation by means of getreply (see clause 22.3.4) and catch (see clause 22.3.6) operations.
requirements.canonical: In blocking procedure-based communication, responses and exceptions to a call ARE handled in the response and exception handling part of the `call` operation by means of `getreply` and `catch` operations.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- In case of blocking procedure-based communication, the handling of responses or exceptions to a call is done in the response and exception handling part of the call operation by means of getreply (see clause 22.3.4) and catch (see clause 22.3.6) operations.

requirements.original: It defines a set of alternatives, describing the possible responses and exceptions to the call.
requirements.canonical: The response and exception handling part of a `call` operation defines a set of alternatives describing the possible responses and exceptions to the call.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- It defines a set of alternatives, describing the possible responses and exceptions to the call.

requirements.original: If necessary, it is possible to enable/disable an alternative by means of a boolean expression placed between the "[ ]" brackets of the alternative.
requirements.canonical: An alternative of the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation MAY be enabled or disabled by a Boolean expression placed between the "[ ]" brackets of the alternative.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- If necessary, it is possible to enable/disable an alternative by means of a boolean expression placed between the "[ ]" brackets of the alternative.

requirements.original: The response and exception handling part of a call operation is executed like an alt statement without any active default.
requirements.canonical: The response and exception handling part of a `call` operation IS executed like an `alt` statement without any active default.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- The response and exception handling part of a call operation is executed like an alt statement without any active default.

requirements.original: This means a corresponding snapshot includes all information necessary to evaluate the (optional) Boolean guards, may include the top element (if any) of the port over which the procedure has been called and may include a timeout exception generated by the (optional) timer that supervises the call.
requirements.canonical: A snapshot taken for the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation includes all information necessary to evaluate the Boolean guards.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- This means a corresponding snapshot includes all information necessary to evaluate the (optional) Boolean guards, may include the top element (if any) of the port over which the procedure has been called and may include a timeout exception generated by the (optional) timer that supervises the call.

requirements.original: This means a corresponding snapshot includes all information necessary to evaluate the (optional) Boolean guards, may include the top element (if any) of the port over which the procedure has been called and may include a timeout exception generated by the (optional) timer that supervises the call.
requirements.canonical: A snapshot taken for the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation MAY include the top element of the port over which the procedure has been called, if any.

ambiguity.issue: 'may include' could mean the snapshot only contains the port top element if present, or that inclusion is optional for the tool; the reading 'includes it if present' is chosen.
readings: A snapshot for the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation SHALL include the top element of the calling port if the queue is not empty.
A snapshot for the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation MAY optionally include the top element of the calling port.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- This means a corresponding snapshot includes all information necessary to evaluate the (optional) Boolean guards, may include the top element (if any) of the port over which the procedure has been called and may include a timeout exception generated by the (optional) timer that supervises the call.

requirements.original: This means a corresponding snapshot includes all information necessary to evaluate the (optional) Boolean guards, may include the top element (if any) of the port over which the procedure has been called and may include a timeout exception generated by the (optional) timer that supervises the call.
requirements.canonical: A snapshot taken for the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation MAY include a timeout exception generated by the timer supervising the call, if such a timer is used.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- This means a corresponding snapshot includes all information necessary to evaluate the (optional) Boolean guards, may include the top element (if any) of the port over which the procedure has been called and may include a timeout exception generated by the (optional) timer that supervises the call.

requirements.original: The call operation may optionally include a timeout.
requirements.canonical: A `call` operation MAY include a timeout value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- The call operation may optionally include a timeout.

requirements.original: This is defined as an explicit value or constant of float type and defines the length of time after the call operation has started that a timeout exception shall be generated by the test system.
requirements.canonical: The timeout value of a `call` operation SHALL be an explicit value or constant of float type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- This is defined as an explicit value or constant of float type and defines the length of time after the call operation has started that a timeout exception shall be generated by the test system.

requirements.original: This is defined as an explicit value or constant of float type and defines the length of time after the call operation has started that a timeout exception shall be generated by the test system.
requirements.canonical: When a timeout value is given in a `call` operation, the test system SHALL generate a timeout exception when the given length of time has elapsed after the `call` operation has started.
requirements.condition: a timeout value is present in the call operation
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- This is defined as an explicit value or constant of float type and defines the length of time after the call operation has started that a timeout exception shall be generated by the test system.

requirements.original: If no timeout value part is present in the call operation, no timeout exception shall be generated.
requirements.canonical: If no timeout value part is present in a `call` operation, the test system SHALL NOT generate a timeout exception for the call.
requirements.condition: no timeout value is present in the call operation
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- If no timeout value part is present in the call operation, no timeout exception shall be generated.

requirements.original: Using the keyword nowait instead of a timeout exception value in a call operation allows calling a procedure to continue without waiting either for a response or an exception raised by the called procedure or a timeout exception.
requirements.canonical: When the keyword `nowait` is used instead of a timeout value in a `call` operation, the calling test component continues execution without waiting for a response, an exception raised by the called procedure, or a timeout exception.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- Using the keyword nowait instead of a timeout exception value in a call operation allows calling a procedure to continue without waiting either for a response or an exception raised by the called procedure or a timeout exception.

requirements.original: If the nowait keyword is used, a possible response or exception of the called procedure has to be removed from the port queue by using a getreply or a catch operation in a subsequent alt statement.
requirements.canonical: If the `nowait` keyword is used in a `call` operation, a response or exception of the called procedure SHALL be removed from the port queue by a `getreply` or `catch` operation in a subsequent `alt` statement.

ambiguity.issue: Unclear whether this is a requirement on the test writer (error if not removed) or a description of the only way to remove such entries; the description reading is chosen as primary.
readings: A response or exception to a `nowait` call can only be removed from the port queue by a `getreply` or `catch` operation in a subsequent `alt` statement.
A test SHALL handle every response or exception of a `nowait` call in a subsequent `alt` statement, otherwise an error occurs.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- If the nowait keyword is used, a possible response or exception of the called procedure has to be removed from the port queue by using a getreply or a catch operation in a subsequent alt statement.

requirements.original: A blocking procedure may have no return values, no out and inout parameters and may raise no exception.
requirements.canonical: A blocking procedure MAY have no return value, no out and inout parameters and raise no exception.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- A blocking procedure may have no return values, no out and inout parameters and may raise no exception.

requirements.original: The call operation for such a procedure shall also have a response and exception handling part to handle the blocking in a uniform manner.
requirements.canonical: A `call` operation of a blocking procedure without return value, out parameters, inout parameters and exceptions SHALL have a response and exception handling part.
requirements.condition: the called procedure is blocking and has no return value, out/inout parameters or exceptions
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- The call operation for such a procedure shall also have a response and exception handling part to handle the blocking in a uniform manner.

requirements.original: A non-blocking procedure has no out and inout parameters, no return value and the non-blocking property is indicated in the corresponding signature definition by means of a noblock keyword.
requirements.canonical: A non-blocking procedure SHALL NOT have out parameters, inout parameters or a return value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- A non-blocking procedure has no out and inout parameters, no return value and the non-blocking property is indicated in the corresponding signature definition by means of a noblock keyword.

requirements.original: A non-blocking procedure has no out and inout parameters, no return value and the non-blocking property is indicated in the corresponding signature definition by means of a noblock keyword.
requirements.canonical: The non-blocking property of a procedure IS indicated in its signature definition by the `noblock` keyword.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- A non-blocking procedure has no out and inout parameters, no return value and the non-blocking property is indicated in the corresponding signature definition by means of a noblock keyword.

requirements.original: Possible exceptions raised by non-blocking procedures have to be removed from the port queue by using catch operations in subsequent alt or interleave statements.
requirements.canonical: An exception raised by a non-blocking procedure SHALL be removed from the port queue by a `catch` operation in a subsequent `alt` or `interleave` statement.

ambiguity.issue: Same as for nowait calls: obligation on the test writer vs. description of the only removal mechanism; obligation reading chosen.
readings: An exception raised by a non-blocking procedure SHALL be removed by a `catch` operation in a subsequent `alt` or `interleave` statement.
An exception raised by a non-blocking procedure CAN only be removed from the port queue by a `catch` operation in a subsequent `alt` or `interleave` statement.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- Possible exceptions raised by non-blocking procedures have to be removed from the port queue by using catch operations in subsequent alt or interleave statements.

requirements.original: Like for the send operation, TTCN-3 also supports unicast, multicast and broadcast calls of procedures.
requirements.canonical: The `call` operation supports unicast, multicast and broadcast calls of procedures, like the `send` operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- Like for the send operation, TTCN-3 also supports unicast, multicast and broadcast calls of procedures.

requirements.original: This can be done in the same manner as described in clause 22.2.1, i.e. the argument of the to clause of a call operation is for unicast calls the address of one receiving entity (or can be omitted in case of one-to-one connections), for multicast calls a list of addresses of a set of receivers and for broadcast calls the all component keyword.
requirements.canonical: For a unicast call, the argument of the `to` clause of a `call` operation IS the address of one receiving entity.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- This can be done in the same manner as described in clause 22.2.1, i.e. the argument of the to clause of a call operation is for unicast calls the address of one receiving entity (or can be omitted in case of one-to-one connections), for multicast calls a list of addresses of a set of receivers and for broadcast calls the all component keyword.

requirements.original: This can be done in the same manner as described in clause 22.2.1, i.e. the argument of the to clause of a call operation is for unicast calls the address of one receiving entity (or can be omitted in case of one-to-one connections), for multicast calls a list of addresses of a set of receivers and for broadcast calls the all component keyword.
requirements.canonical: For a multicast call, the argument of the `to` clause of a `call` operation IS a list of addresses of a set of receivers.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- This can be done in the same manner as described in clause 22.2.1, i.e. the argument of the to clause of a call operation is for unicast calls the address of one receiving entity (or can be omitted in case of one-to-one connections), for multicast calls a list of addresses of a set of receivers and for broadcast calls the all component keyword.

requirements.original: This can be done in the same manner as described in clause 22.2.1, i.e. the argument of the to clause of a call operation is for unicast calls the address of one receiving entity (or can be omitted in case of one-to-one connections), for multicast calls a list of addresses of a set of receivers and for broadcast calls the all component keyword.
requirements.canonical: For a broadcast call, the argument of the `to` clause of a `call` operation IS the `all component` keyword.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- This can be done in the same manner as described in clause 22.2.1, i.e. the argument of the to clause of a call operation is for unicast calls the address of one receiving entity (or can be omitted in case of one-to-one connections), for multicast calls a list of addresses of a set of receivers and for broadcast calls the all component keyword.

requirements.original: In case of one-to-one connections, the to clause may be omitted, because the receiving entity is uniquely identified by the system structure.
requirements.canonical: In case of a one-to-one connection, the `to` clause of a `call` operation MAY be omitted, because the receiving entity is uniquely identified by the system structure.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- In case of one-to-one connections, the to clause may be omitted, because the receiving entity is uniquely identified by the system structure.

requirements.original: A multicast or broadcast call operation may cause several responses and exceptions from different communication partners.
requirements.canonical: A multicast or broadcast `call` operation CAN cause several responses and exceptions from different communication partners.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- A multicast or broadcast call operation may cause several responses and exceptions from different communication partners.

requirements.original: In case of a multicast or broadcast call operation of a non-blocking procedure, all exceptions which may be raised from the different communication partners can be handled in subsequent catch, alt or interleave statements.
requirements.canonical: For a multicast or broadcast `call` operation of a non-blocking procedure, all exceptions raised by the different communication partners CAN be handled in subsequent `catch` operations, `alt` or `interleave` statements.
requirements.condition: multicast or broadcast call of a non-blocking procedure
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- In case of a multicast or broadcast call operation of a non-blocking procedure, all exceptions which may be raised from the different communication partners can be handled in subsequent catch, alt or interleave statements.

requirements.original: In case of a multicast or broadcast call operation of a blocking procedure, responses and exceptions can be handled in several ways: one possibility is to handle only one response or exception in the response and exception handling part of the call operation.
requirements.canonical: For a multicast or broadcast `call` operation of a blocking procedure, the response and exception handling part of the `call` operation MAY handle only one response or exception.
requirements.condition: multicast or broadcast call of a blocking procedure
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- In case of a multicast or broadcast call operation of a blocking procedure, responses and exceptions can be handled in several ways: one possibility is to handle only one response or exception in the response and exception handling part of the call operation.

requirements.original: All further responses and exceptions are handled in subsequent alt or interleave statements.
requirements.canonical: When only one response or exception of a multicast or broadcast blocking call is handled in the response and exception handling part, all further responses and exceptions ARE handled in subsequent `alt` or `interleave` statements.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- All further responses and exceptions are handled in subsequent alt or interleave statements.

requirements.original: Alternatively, several or all responses and exceptions are processed in the response and exception handling part of the call operation by means of nested alt statements or by using the repeat operation causing the re-evaluation of the call body.
requirements.canonical: For a multicast or broadcast `call` operation of a blocking procedure, several or all responses and exceptions MAY be processed in the response and exception handling part by nested `alt` statements or by the `repeat` operation, which causes re-evaluation of the call body.
requirements.condition: multicast or broadcast call of a blocking procedure
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- Alternatively, several or all responses and exceptions are processed in the response and exception handling part of the call operation by means of nested alt statements or by using the repeat operation causing the re-evaluation of the call body.

requirements.original: A further possibility is to use the nowait directive and to handle all responses and exceptions in subsequent alt or interleave statements.
requirements.canonical: For a multicast or broadcast `call` operation of a blocking procedure, the `nowait` keyword MAY be used and all responses and exceptions handled in subsequent `alt` or `interleave` statements.
requirements.condition: multicast or broadcast call of a blocking procedure
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- A further possibility is to use the nowait directive and to handle all responses and exceptions in subsequent alt or interleave statements.

requirements.original: a) The call operation shall only be used on procedure-based ports.
requirements.canonical: The `call` operation SHALL only be used on procedure-based ports.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- a) The call operation shall only be used on procedure-based ports.

requirements.original: The type definition of the port shall include the name of the procedure to which the call operation belongs in its out or inout list i.e. it shall be allowed to call this procedure at this port.
requirements.canonical: The port type definition of the port used in a `call` operation SHALL include the signature of the called procedure in its out or inout list.

ambiguity.issue: 'name of the procedure' is used where 'signature' is meant; 'out or inout list' refers to the out/inout direction lists of the port type.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- The type definition of the port shall include the name of the procedure to which the call operation belongs in its out or inout list i.e. it shall be allowed to call this procedure at this port.

requirements.original: b) All in and inout parameters of the signature shall have a specific value i.e. the use of matching mechanisms such as AnyValue is not allowed.
requirements.canonical: All in and inout parameters of the signature used in a `call` operation SHALL have a specific value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- b) All in and inout parameters of the signature shall have a specific value i.e. the use of matching mechanisms such as AnyValue is not allowed.

requirements.original: b) All in and inout parameters of the signature shall have a specific value i.e. the use of matching mechanisms such as AnyValue is not allowed.
requirements.canonical: A matching mechanism such as AnyValue SHALL NOT be used for in and inout parameters of the signature in a `call` operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- b) All in and inout parameters of the signature shall have a specific value i.e. the use of matching mechanisms such as AnyValue is not allowed.

requirements.original: c) Only out parameters may be omitted or specified with a matching attribute.
requirements.canonical: In a `call` operation, only out parameters of the signature MAY be omitted or specified with a matching mechanism.

ambiguity.issue: 'matching attribute' is used instead of 'matching mechanism'; 'omitted' refers to the not-used symbol '-'.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- c) Only out parameters may be omitted or specified with a matching attribute.

requirements.original: d) The signature arguments of the call operation are not used to retrieve variable names for out and inout parameters.
requirements.canonical: The signature arguments of a `call` operation ARE NOT used to retrieve variable names for out and inout parameters.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- d) The signature arguments of the call operation are not used to retrieve variable names for out and inout parameters.

requirements.original: The actual assignment of the procedure return value and out and inout parameter values to variables shall explicitly be made in the response and exception handling part of the call operation by means of getreply and catch operations.
requirements.canonical: The assignment of the procedure return value and of out and inout parameter values to variables SHALL be made explicitly in the response and exception handling part of the `call` operation by `getreply` and `catch` operations.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- The actual assignment of the procedure return value and out and inout parameter values to variables shall explicitly be made in the response and exception handling part of the call operation by means of getreply and catch operations.

requirements.original: This allows the use of signature templates in call operations in the same manner as templates can be used for types.
requirements.canonical: Signature templates MAY be used in `call` operations in the same manner as templates are used for types.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- This allows the use of signature templates in call operations in the same manner as templates can be used for types.

requirements.original: e) A to clause shall be present in case of one-to-many connections.
requirements.canonical: A `to` clause SHALL be present in a `call` operation in case of one-to-many connections.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.1 -- e) A to clause shall be present in case of one-to-many connections.
